title: Pascha
hook: Christ is risen! Truly he is risen!

segments.voice: Yesterday, Great Lent, which begins on a Monday after everyone bows and asks forgiveness. Your line was clean monday.

Near midnight, and the church is dark. Not dim. Dark. Everyone is holding an unlit candle. Then the priest comes out from behind the icon screen holding a single flame, and the light starts to travel, his candle to the first person's, theirs to the next, until the whole room is gold and flickering. The people follow him outside and walk around the church in the night air, singing. At the closed front doors, the priest calls out a short greeting, and the crowd shouts back an answer, loud enough to wake the street. Then the doors open, and Lent is over.
screen: `A DARK CHURCH, ONE FLAME.` → `AROUND THE CHURCH, SINGING.` → `THE DOORS OPEN.`

segments.voice: Pascha is what Eastern Christians call Easter. Paul ties it straight to the Passover lamb: in the Douay-Rheims, "For Christ our pasch is sacrificed." The pasch is the Passover. Easter, for these churches, is the new Passover, the night God leads his people from death into life. Then the greeting. Christ is risen! Truly he is risen! It's said in Greek, Arabic, Ukrainian, Malayalam, Ge'ez, the languages of the churches we've visited. The answer isn't decoration. It echoes the first Easter evening in Luke, when the disciples tell each other, "The Lord is risen indeed." Indeed. Truly. It's a witness, said back. And people keep saying it, as a hello and a goodbye, through the Easter season. Then the hymn they sing outside the doors, which the Byzantine churches repeat over and over: Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and giving life to those in the tombs. Last, a sermon read aloud at the midnight liturgy, attributed to Saint John Chrysostom. It invites everyone to the feast: those who fasted the whole of Lent, those who came at the last hour, and those who didn't fast at all. Nobody should go away hungry, it says. Nobody should mourn their failings, because forgiveness has risen from the tomb. After a strict Lent, that's not the moment to check who kept the rules. The table is set for all.
screen: `CHRIST OUR PASCH: THE NEW PASSOVER.` · `TRULY HE IS RISEN: A WITNESS SAID BACK.` · `TRAMPLING DOWN DEATH BY DEATH.` · `THE TABLE IS SET FOR ALL.` · then, large: `THE LORD IS RISEN INDEED.`

segments.voice: Say the greeting quietly a few times, Christ is risen, truly he is risen, letting the second line come a little stronger, the way a crowd answers. Picture someone you could greet this way at Easter, a friend, a grandparent, someone in a parish hall, and their face as they answer. If you pray, the greeting itself can be your prayer; if you don't, hold it as a sentence shouted at midnight in many languages, and notice how it lands.
Pascha. The Eastern name for Easter, the new Passover, the feast of Christ's resurrection, opened at midnight with candles and a shouted greeting. Today's word.
Your line: truly he is risen. It's a witness, said back a little stronger. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Eastern Catholics celebrate Pascha at a night service with candles, a procession around the church and the repeated greeting "Christ is risen! Truly he is risen!", and use the greeting in place of hello throughout the Easter season.

chat.says: At a Ukrainian church, someone said Christ is risen and waited. What was I supposed to say?
options: Truly he is risen. It's the Easter answer, a witness said back, like Luke's the Lord is risen indeed.
Happy Easter to you. The greeting is only a polite hello, so any friendly reply will do fine.
Amen, and nothing more. In Eastern churches the answer is always one quiet word, never shouted.

notes: Paschal troparion given in a common English form ('Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and giving life to those in the tombs') without quotation marks, since English wordings vary. Confirm it is acceptable as a description.
Paschal homily of Chrysostom summarized, not quoted. Confirm the summary.
The greeting's use 'for the whole Easter season' (until Ascension in Byzantine practice): confirm.
Midnight service description (dark church, light from behind the iconostasis, procession, closed doors) follows common Byzantine practice; details vary. Confirm.
The link between Pascha and Passover is made through 1 Corinthians 5:7 rather than an etymology. Confirm.
Douay-Rheims wording of 1 Corinthians 5:7 and Luke 24:34: confirm.
Original: Χριστὸς ἀνέστη / Ἀληθῶς ἀνέστη; confirm accents and pronunciation.
